			o Mike (UNMC rep) will discuss with the lab for resolution
	· Logic behind the flat file report requires a certain encounter (current list of encounter types noted in the thread below) to occur within the last week, it then pulls results for measures setup in the file regardless of date, here are a few issues identified using the current logic
			o If a member has the lab work alone, an encounter (out to the list below) does not occur, the query logic doesn’t pick-up that result
					§ Mike could add lab encounters to the logic, he has sent an estimation of how many rows this will add to the report (approximately 500), I’m assuming we can handle the addition of 500 rows but wanted to verify that with you
			o If a member has a qualifying encounter type but the lab result does not occur on that date the logic will not pull the result until the member has one of the encounter types noted below 
					§ Example: patient seen on 07.01.20 for an office visit, A1C results on 07.02.20, logic pulls results dated 07.01.20 and before. We would not get this result on a flat file until the next qualifying encounter type
					§ Some of these could likely be captured if telephone encounters were one of the qualifying encounter types but this will double the row count (current row count is ~9-10K), i confirmed that we can accept all of the data they have to send as long as they do not change the flat file and that 2021 may be a good time to discuss CCD submissions.

​9/4/20 SW: To All,
I wanted to follow up on the question coming out of our 8/24 meeting related to the processing of Koan Health data by other payors.  We’ve met with our HEDIS audit team and they have indicated that we can’t move forward until Koan obtains NCQA certification.   We can’t speak to the other payors but we feel that our process is fully compliant with existing HEDIS guidelines.    Our audit team has also indicated there are a number of upcoming changes to the certification process and that NCQA is building a new program called Data Aggregator Validation (DAV) that will be launched in 2021 for reporting in 2022.  We will continue to monitor these changes and it’s our expectation going forward that all data aggregators will go through the DAV process as a prerequisite for data transmission to UHC.

Regards,
Eric C. Schmidt

01-21-2025 bjp: rec'd notification regarding SN ticket RITM5889060 to re-activate ECG stating "ECG Config has been activated"; sent f/u email to submitter informing "I have received notification the support tickets to have the interface and SFTP connection re-activated has been completed. You may proceed with submitting a Production file at this time."; will await file submission

01-21-2025 bjp: sent f/u email to submitter stating "I hope you had a wonderful weekend! In reviewing the information you requested, I realized I did not provide the file format information for you. I have attached a copy of the “Submitter Profile” which was completed for your organization. Please note the information on tabs labeled “Flat File Format Requirements” and “FF ONLY_UHC Layout Information”. Below I have highlighted some important details: Standard Flat File: 1) ASCII text files (*.txt); 2) Pipe delimited files; 3) CRLF record terminator; 4) No spaces, NUL, or NULL in blank fields; 5) No blank rows or extra record terminators after last record (row); 6) UTF-8 character encoding; 7) File MUST contain all 120 columns outlined in the layout even if column has no data; 8) All columns MUST match field name exactly AND in the same order (even if the column/field does not have a value populated). As always, please let me know if you have any questions."

01-21-2025 bjp: rec'd notification regarding SN ticket INC41114513 to re-activate interface stating "Verified the prod configuration and re activated the Interface."; awaiting re-activation of ECG connection

01-17-2025 bjp: rec'd email from submitter stating "Do you have the documentation for submission requirements? 1) (column datatypes, character lengths, etc.) 2) Submission location, the site and what is needed to access it"; sent f/u email stating "I have attached a copy of the headers we received in your test file that was approved last year. Please make sure to follow the configured format as well as the naming convention or the file will be rejected. Here is the naming convention used for the Test file: MO_OCH_TEST_UHC_20230101_20231231.txt. Please remember to change ‘TEST’ to ‘PROD’ in the filename (see example below). This is how our system knows to push it into the Production environment. Ex: MO_OCH_TEST_UHC_20230101_20231231.txt, MO_OCH_PROD_UHC_20230101_20231231.txt. I have also attached a copy of the Section 5 documentation we received. Please review this information and let me know if you have any changes/updates. This information is REQUIRED for all supplemental data submissions and must be up-to-date per NCQA requirements. Please let me know if you have any further questions."; awaiting completion of SN ticket to re-activate the ECG-sftp connection and another SN ticket to re-activate the interface

01-16-2025 bjp: entered SN ticket INC41114513 to re-activate interface

01-16-2025 bjp: rec'd email from Karl w/ submitter stating "OCH is interested in setting up our supplemental data feed for Optum / UHC to close 2024 year care gaps if possible. The last email I have from Billie was on 5/17 about us setting up the UHC supplemental data feed. I saw the Optum logo in their signature and thought to include them on this email in case it was relevant. What step in the process are we in? 12/8/2021 - Call scheduled for 1/12/2022 to review CDSM E2E w/ IRIS-SDR

12/7/2021 - Call scheduled for 1/13/2022 to revisit CDSM/BioMetrics Interface updates.  This will be considered a 2022 priority item and potential reprocessing request.
The only measures that are mapped currently are BMI, BP and A1c. When they were first implemented, we simply did not receive the codes that would need to be hard coded for the other fields in the file. They do not send LOINCS in their file(s). This is in process of being remedied with the work we are doing with the Biometrics team. They have 2 file formats, one a 31-field file and one a 71-field file. They want us to take both. We are working on doing that (this will require multiple interfaces). Once that work is completed, the remaining analytes will flow downstream to SDR.
We’re looking at Feb/March 2022 for completion due to some resource constraints at the moment (we are revisiting with the Biometrics team in January). Since the current structure is 31-field, we should be able to reprocess the original files..

11/30/2021 - Completed BioMetrics DTL change request call with Optum BioMetrics team, eVisor team, and CDSM.  It was determined that DTL changes looking to be moved to production will need to be delayed until atleast January 2022,  so that Optum BioMetrics team can account for changes requested.  It was suggested to have multiple interfaces to account for the different file types - a 71 field DTL (new data analyte layout for Quest) and a 31 field DTL (existing file layout for all other vendors).  
Discussed solution: Dawns team may create a translation which will map the 31 field formats to the new format. New clients will be mapped to the 71 field format. Her team does not have capacity to do this development in 2021.
Decision: the new format will not be implemented this year.  Files without the new layout will not be loaded into CDSM.

Dawn Gundersen will take lead on any development efforts and work with Jon L to ensure things are done correctly.  Layne R. and Deepak G. did not share new data analyte file layout requests with Dawn G and team.  Deb Levy will be replacing Layne R..

07-02-2024 bjp: rec'd QA review notification and report stating "We received sign off from QA Validation for Mercy(63). I would request you to check the attached QA report and share feedback if any before we could proceed with next steps."; during EAAM mtg, Jon reported this will be promoted to PROD soon

06-19-2024 bjp: rec'd email from submitter stating "We’ve removed the custom codes from our supplemental data submissions to UHC.  You should only be receiving CPT/CPT2 codes."; sent f/u email to Jon and team informing of this information

06-18-2024 bjp: rec'd email from submitter on 6/14 stating "We are questioning why a result is required for COL lab results to count? In the file submission specs, PosNegResult and Lab Numeric Result Value fields are “C” (required conditional – measure relevant requirement). 1) Because the COL measure compliance is dependent upon the screening being completed, and not the results of the screening, why is some result being required?; As opposed to A1c, for example, where compliance is dependent upon the result (either value or cpt2); The LOINC codes are in the value sets and thus should satisfy compliance, right?; Additionally, for external labs we don’t get the results. Just that the screening was performed/completed. If you can provide more information on the requirements, that would be helpful so that we can make sure we are getting credit for completed screenings."; per email rec'd from Jon/Venkat "We were able to send LOINC codes without result value to downstream."; sent f/u email to submitter stating "I have reached out to several colleagues/departments to get feedback on your question. Based on the responses I have received at this time, the LOINC code for a COL measure without a result is acceptable and will be sent downstream to the HEDIS engine for processing. With this being said, the current Test files we have on file will continue to move through the QA process. You do NOT need to send another Test file."; will await additional QA results

06-18-2024 bjp: rec'd notification during EAAM the previous test files received can be used to proceed with QA process; QDM will notify submitter

06-04-2024 bjp: rec'd Second level review notification, all 4 files failed due to "LOINC codes with empty lab results"; this is also occurring in current PROD files and majority of issue appears to be for COL measure only; the following findings were provided by Jon via email "I looked at the Mercy files we discussed this morning to see if they are currently sending with no lab results. They are currently sending blank results for some labs. These are from their last submitted production files (1/9/2024) for each facility. 1) CID 63 Mercy Arkansas has 54275 records. Of that, 29820 records have LOINC codes.1682 of those records have no result values. 2) CID 820 Mercy Springfield has 117269 records. Of that, 56668 have LOINC codes. 4311 of those records have no result values. 3) CID 887 Mercy Oklahoma has 90408 records. Of that, 45819 records have LOINC codes. 3908 of those have no result values. 4) CID 889 Mercy East has 369627 records. Of that 168892 records have LOINC codes. 1886 of those records have no result values. While these number are small, it could still potentially have an effect on both STARS and HEDIS® ratings."; sent f/u email to submitter informing "During second level QA review of the TEST files listed below, our internal team has determined ALL of these files have failed due to "LOINC codes with empty lab results". 
CID	Campaign Name	Test File Name
889	MERCY MEDICAL GROUP/East	CDS_634126692_001_000_mercy_east_PrimaryCare_TEST_all_20240405.txt
 820	 MERCY MEDICAL GROUP/Springfield	 CDS_636563799_001_000_mercy_Springfield_PrimaryCare_TEST_20240405.txt
 63	 Mercy	 CDS_636472859_001_000_mercy_Arkansas_PrimaryCare_TEST_20240405.txt
887	 Mercy Health System Oklahoma	 CDS_636572551_001_000_mercy_Oklahoma_PrimaryCare_TEST_20240405.txt
 In addition, we reviewed the Production files sent on 1/9/2023 for each facility to see if there were any issues with LOINC codes. It appears the majority of the records with “no result values” are for the COL measure. While these number are small, it could still potentially have an effect on both STARS and HEDIS® ratings. Here are the results: 1) CID 63 Mercy Arkansas has 54275 records; 29820 records have LOINC codes, 1682 of those records have no result values; 2) CID 820 Mercy Springfield has 117269 records; 56668 have LOINC codes, 4311 of those records have no result values; 3) CID 887 Mercy Oklahoma has 90408 records; 45819 records have LOINC codes, 3908 of those have no result values; 4) CID 889 Mercy East has 369627 records; 168892 records have LOINC codes, 1886 of those records have no result values. Please correct the issue and resubmit a new Test file for each facility. It is recommended a new Test file be received within the next 2 weeks. If we do not receive a Test file within this timeframe, we cannot guarantee the resources allocated to your implementation will be readily available. This means your Test file will ‘move to the back of the line’ and may take longer to be reviewed ultimately extending your implementation timeline. Please let me know if there are any questions as I am happy to help."

05-24-2024 bjp: rec'd Test File Review email  stating "We were verified the Mercy data, the submitter is sending the results in three separate columns (Result, pos_neg_rslt and lab_result_text) and few empty values. Please notify the submitter to do not send LOINC codes with empty lab results and we will be documenting this in our QA report as well and find the below details for more information."; sent f/u email to submitter informing "This is a follow up regarding the Test files submitted for all 4 Mercy accounts. I have received additional feedback from our team reviewing the Test files. Please review and correct these issues to alleviate any potential quality issues moving forward: 1) Results were found in three separate columns (Result, pos_neg_rslt and lab_result_text) and few empty values, As noted below from the file specs, “For a lab result being submitted, either a numeric result, pos/neg result, OR lab text resultare required. Do not duplicate values in multiple columns.”; 2) DO NOT send LOINC codes with empty lab results, If a LOINC is noted but NO lab result is found associated with the code, this will cause the data to be dropped and will not apply to the care gap measure."; will await further QA results

05-14-2024 bjp: per EAAM notes "they have logic to convert the CPT codes currently", Jon needs to know if they will be sending in CPT codes without translating; sent email to submitter stating "In reviewing the Test files submitted, there is a question regarding the custom codes you previously submitted in 2023. Please let us know what to expect in this New file format. 1) Will you continue to submit the custom codes (“local codes mapped to a CPT”)? 2) OR, will you be only sending CPT/CPT2 codes?"; will await response

05-14-2024 bjp:  rec'd Test File Review email, passed File Review; findings that needs to be corrected include: 1) Member City - 24816 records have values. No blanks. There are 4 records with numeric value like zipcode (72940) instead of City; 2) CPT Code - 10471 records have values. There is 1 CPT2Code(0501F) received in CPT Code column. 14345 records are blank; sent f/u email to submitter informing Test file passed first level review and shared findings to be corrected; will await further QA results

05-07-2024 bjp: rec'd notification test file was submitted, Filenames: mercy_Arkansas_PrimaryCare_TEST_20240405.txt; sent email notification to Jon and team; will await QA results

05-02-2024 bjp: rec'd notification file failed d/t "File received with only 119 columns. One column is missing in the middle on the layouts and the column is “QUANTITYOFSERVICE” which is in 64th position in the standard layout and the data for this column is optional."; sent email to submitter; will await response

04-29-2024 bjp: rec'd notification test files have been submitted, Filenames: mercy_east_PrimaryCare_TEST_all_20240404.txt, mercy_Arkansas_PrimaryCare_TEST_20240404.txt, mercy_Oklahoma_PrimaryCare_TEST_20240404.txt, mercy_Springfield_PrimaryCare_TEST_20240404.txt; sent email notification to Jon and team; will await QA results

06-18-2024 bjp: rec'd email from submitter on 6/14 stating "We are questioning why a result is required for COL lab results to count? In the file submission specs, PosNegResult and Lab Numeric Result Value fields are “C” (required conditional – measure relevant requirement). 1) Because the COL measure compliance is dependent upon the screening being completed, and not the results of the screening, why is some result being required?; As opposed to A1c, for example, where compliance is dependent upon the result (either value or cpt2); The LOINC codes are in the value sets and thus should satisfy compliance, right?; Additionally, for external labs we don’t get the results. Just that the screening was performed/completed. If you can provide more information on the requirements, that would be helpful so that we can make sure we are getting credit for completed screenings."; per email rec'd from Jon/Venkat "We were able to send LOINC codes without result value to downstream."; sent f/u email to submitter stating "I have reached out to several colleagues/departments to get feedback on your question. Based on the responses I have received at this time, the LOINC code for a COL measure without a result is acceptable and will be sent downstream to the HEDIS engine for processing. With this being said, the current Test files we have on file will continue to move through the QA process. You do NOT need to send another Test file."; will await additional QA results

06-18-2024 bjp: rec'd notification during EAAM the previous test files received can be used to proceed with QA process; QDM will notify submitter

06-04-2024 bjp: rec'd Second level review notification, all 4 files failed due to "LOINC codes with empty lab results"; this is also occurring in current PROD files and majority of issue appears to be for COL measure only; the following findings were provided by Jon via email "I looked at the Mercy files we discussed this morning to see if they are currently sending with no lab results. They are currently sending blank results for some labs. These are from their last submitted production files (1/9/2024) for each facility. 1) CID 63 Mercy Arkansas has 54275 records. Of that, 29820 records have LOINC codes.1682 of those records have no result values. 2) CID 820 Mercy Springfield has 117269 records. Of that, 56668 have LOINC codes. 4311 of those records have no result values. 3) CID 887 Mercy Oklahoma has 90408 records. Of that, 45819 records have LOINC codes. 3908 of those have no result values. 4) CID 889 Mercy East has 369627 records. Of that 168892 records have LOINC codes. 1886 of those records have no result values. While these number are small, it could still potentially have an effect on both STARS and HEDIS® ratings."; sent f/u email to submitter informing "During second level QA review of the TEST files listed below, our internal team has determined ALL of these files have failed due to "LOINC codes with empty lab results". 
CID	Campaign Name	Test File Name
889	MERCY MEDICAL GROUP/East	CDS_634126692_001_000_mercy_east_PrimaryCare_TEST_all_20240405.txt
 820	 MERCY MEDICAL GROUP/Springfield	 CDS_636563799_001_000_mercy_Springfield_PrimaryCare_TEST_20240405.txt
 63	 Mercy	 CDS_636472859_001_000_mercy_Arkansas_PrimaryCare_TEST_20240405.txt
887	 Mercy Health System Oklahoma	 CDS_636572551_001_000_mercy_Oklahoma_PrimaryCare_TEST_20240405.txt
 In addition, we reviewed the Production files sent on 1/9/2023 for each facility to see if there were any issues with LOINC codes. It appears the majority of the records with “no result values” are for the COL measure. While these number are small, it could still potentially have an effect on both STARS and HEDIS® ratings. Here are the results: 1) CID 63 Mercy Arkansas has 54275 records; 29820 records have LOINC codes, 1682 of those records have no result values; 2) CID 820 Mercy Springfield has 117269 records; 56668 have LOINC codes, 4311 of those records have no result values; 3) CID 887 Mercy Oklahoma has 90408 records; 45819 records have LOINC codes, 3908 of those have no result values; 4) CID 889 Mercy East has 369627 records; 168892 records have LOINC codes, 1886 of those records have no result values. Please correct the issue and resubmit a new Test file for each facility. It is recommended a new Test file be received within the next 2 weeks. If we do not receive a Test file within this timeframe, we cannot guarantee the resources allocated to your implementation will be readily available. This means your Test file will ‘move to the back of the line’ and may take longer to be reviewed ultimately extending your implementation timeline. Please let me know if there are any questions as I am happy to help."

05-24-2024 bjp: rec'd Test File Review email  stating "We were verified the Mercy data, the submitter is sending the results in three separate columns (Result, pos_neg_rslt and lab_result_text) and few empty values. Please notify the submitter to do not send LOINC codes with empty lab results and we will be documenting this in our QA report as well and find the below details for more information."; sent f/u email to submitter informing "This is a follow up regarding the Test files submitted for all 4 Mercy accounts. I have received additional feedback from our team reviewing the Test files. Please review and correct these issues to alleviate any potential quality issues moving forward: 1) Results were found in three separate columns (Result, pos_neg_rslt and lab_result_text) and few empty values, As noted below from the file specs, “For a lab result being submitted, either a numeric result, pos/neg result, OR lab text resultare required. Do not duplicate values in multiple columns.”; 2) DO NOT send LOINC codes with empty lab results, If a LOINC is noted but NO lab result is found associated with the code, this will cause the data to be dropped and will not apply to the care gap measure."; will await further QA results
